answer: An agent named violet buys vine shipments through a jetty exchange. Each supplier locks collateral for a limited number of orders before a random beacon assigns buyers and inspectors. Payment requires a unique shipment receipt signed at departure and arrival; transfers among linked accounts do not build reputation. Inspectors compare unpredictable sample lots, and provably forged receipts slash the reserved bond. Extra aliases must finance extra collateral and real inspected cargo, so creating accounts alone cannot multiply rewards or voting weight.
